item.title: Implement ledger.py per SPEC.md with locking and focused tests (adaptive)
item.brief:
Operator request (authenticated local socket): "Implement `ledger.py` according to `SPEC.md`. Preserve the documented API, handle every specified error and boundary case, and add focused tests. The existing tests cover basics only. Use the Python standard library and commit your work."

A previous direct-pipeline attempt escalated because SPEC.md requires concurrency control, so this is re-queued on adaptive. That attempt committed nothing; ledger.py is still the NotImplementedError stub on the branch.

Goal: make ledger.py match SPEC.md exactly. Read SPEC.md first and treat it as the contract.

Concurrency requirements from the spec: linearizable transfers across threads, snapshots that never see a half-transfer, and deadlock-free opposite-direction transfers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every documented public function/class and its signature is preserved; no API changes beyond what SPEC.md states.
- Every error case in SPEC.md raises the specified exception type with the specified behaviour; every boundary case is handled.
- Lock ordering is explicit and documented in code (short comment), so opposite transfers cannot deadlock.
- Tests cover each error path and boundary case, plus concurrency: concurrent transfers preserve totals, opposite-direction transfers complete, and snapshots never observe a half-transfer.
- Only the Python standard library is used.
- Run the full test suite and report results; do not report success if tests fail.
- Keep functions small and readable; validate inputs at the boundary; never swallow exceptions.
- Commit on the item's branch with a clear message. No attribution lines naming AI tools; use the repository's configured git identity only.

pr.body:
Approach: one threading.Lock guards all balances. Each transfer runs as a single critical section (checks and both writes), and snapshot copies under the same lock. With one lock there is no lock ordering to get wrong, so opposite-direction transfers cannot deadlock.

Validation: construction copies the input dict first and then validates the stored copy, so a dict subclass with a lying items() cannot store a bad balance. Ints must be built-in int (bool and int subclasses rejected). Amount is validated before account lookup. Non-string or unknown accounts raise KeyError. Self-transfer returns whether the balance covers the amount and never changes it.

Files: ledger.py, test_ledger.py (existing two tests kept).

Checks: python3 -m unittest on cb83b4c: 27 tests OK. Mutants run in temp copies: lock-free snapshot, lock-free transfer, and isinstance int check each fail the suite. The snapshot-atomicity test pauses a transfer between its debit and credit (PausingDict) and requires a snapshot taken meanwhile to see the completed transfer; it uses a 1 s probe window, so a lock-free snapshot fails it deterministically. Worker joins have timeouts so a deadlock fails tests rather than hanging.

Review scope: whole-change reads of ad0dde1 by three reviewers (verdict fail; both blocking defects fixed in cb83b4c: lying-items bypass, snapshot test not forcing overlap, int-subclass coverage). Delta review of ad0dde1..cb83b4c by one reviewer: pass.

Open non-blocking follow-ups: the opposite-direction test does not assert that any transfer succeeded; _move has no invariant assertion; two blank lines missing before class MyInt in test_ledger.py.

Assumptions and limits: concurrency tests are stress checks, not proofs; the paused-transfer test depends on a 1 s probe window (only affects timing, never produces a false failure on correct code). No external dependencies.
pr.summary: Made Ledger(balances), transfer and snapshot work per SPEC.md. Now: validated construction and amounts, KeyError for unknown accounts, False for insufficient funds or overflow, single-lock atomic transfers, snapshots never see half a transfer. Before: NotImplementedError stub, 2 tests erroring. Now: 27 tests pass.
